tongue-map: The tongue map you learned in school is wrong.
It said sweet lives at the tip and bitter at the back.
It came from a misread German paper, over a century old.
Every part of the tongue that tastes can taste all five.
The differences between regions are tiny.
The map was wrong. Nobody updated the textbook.
mint: Mint isn't cold. It only tells your nerves it is.
Menthol switches on the same sensor that detects cold.
Your mouth stays exactly the same temperature.
That's why water feels icy after a mint.
And a fresh feeling isn't the same as a clean mouth.
Mint isn't cold. It just feels that way.
spicy: Spicy isn't a taste. It's a pain signal.
The capsaicin in chili triggers the nerves that sense heat.
Your tongue reports a burn that isn't happening.
That's why spicy food makes you sweat.
Taste buds handle sweet, sour, salty, bitter and savory.
Spicy isn't a taste. It's your mouth sounding an alarm.
smell: Nobody tells you most of flavor is smell.
Your tongue only handles five basic tastes.
Everything else travels from the mouth up to the nose.
That's why food goes bland when you have a cold.
Try it. Hold your nose and eat a jelly bean.
Sweet, and nothing else. Most of flavor is smell.
airplane: Airplane food isn't as bad as it tastes.
Cabin air is drier than most deserts.
Dry air dulls your nose, and flavor is mostly smell.
Sweet and salty fade the most.
So airlines add extra salt and sugar.
It isn't the food. It's the air.
taste-buds: Your taste buds are about two weeks old.
The cells inside them are replaced every week or two.
That's why a burned tongue recovers in days.
You have thousands of them, and not only on the tongue.
The roof of the mouth and the throat have them too.
Your taste buds are about two weeks old.
saliva: Your mouth makes over a liter of saliva a day.
It rinses away food and keeps bacteria in check.
At night, production slows right down.
That's why mornings taste the way they do.
A glass of water gets the rinse going again.
Over a liter a day, and you never notice.
tongue-step: Nobody tells you to clean your tongue.
Brushing cleans the teeth and skips it.
Bacteria there make much of the odor in breath.
The Romans scraped theirs. Ayurveda still does.
It takes a few seconds each morning.
Nobody taught us the tongue step. Now you know.
